why_it_matters: N controls tensor shape, model input size, and how much history is 'burned' before the first trainable example in each 2-year window; wrong N changes both capacity and effective sample count.

candidate_options.source_support: Common convention for 'one year lookback' in weekly sector-rotation literature; not stated in paper.

candidate_options.description: N = 104 (two full trailing years, matching the annual training-window length)
candidate_options.source_support: Mirrors the paper's explicit '2 years' training-history statement, but that statement describes the *training set span*, not necessarily the *tensor depth* per example.

candidate_options.description: N small (e.g. 4-12 weeks), a short technical-momentum window
candidate_options.source_support: No direct support; included only as the other end of the plausible range.

topic: Which Yahoo Finance price field populates X_t
source_evidence: p.3 says only 'prices... recorded for the current and previous N-1 weeks' were assembled into X_t; never states raw Close vs Adjusted Close vs returns.
why_it_matters: Determines whether corporate actions (splits, dividends) are silently embedded in the model's price history, and whether the network sees levels or returns -- both materially change learned representations.

candidate_options.description: Raw (unadjusted) Friday close
candidate_options.source_support: Matches 'Friday close prices' language literally.

candidate_options.description: Adjusted close (dividend + split adjusted)
candidate_options.source_support: None specific; common practice for ML-on-prices work generally.

candidate_options.description: Week-over-week simple returns computed from Friday closes
candidate_options.source_support: Consistent with 'normalized to zero mean unit variance' framing being easier to justify for returns than for price levels, but not stated.

resolution.option_chosen: B, restated exactly as levels (not returns)
resolution.outcome: RESOLVED by explicit user instruction, not by inference upgrade -- source_classification stays MISSING (the paper never states this field). model_price[s,t] = AdjustedClose[s, final_actual_trading_day_of_week_t], a price LEVEL -- not a return, percent-change, log-return, or window-rebased quantity. User rationale (recorded for provenance): Adjusted Close incorporates dividends/distributions into the historical economic price path and avoids treating stock splits/corporate actions or mechanical ex-dividend drops as artificial price shocks in a sector-ETF universe where distributions are material. Weekly sampling reuses the already-resolved holiday-aware calendar machinery (src/calendar.py's `model_cutoff` = the week's final *actual* trading session, e.g. Thursday Adjusted Close on a Good-Friday week) -- no literal-Friday assumption. Implemented in src/tensors.py::build_weekly_price_matrix. Applies ONLY to the model input tensor.
resolution.note: Does NOT alter the already-resolved target/execution interval (DECISION_REQUIRED_TARGET_RETURN_INTERVAL), which continues to use RAW executable Open (entry) and Close (exit) -- Adjusted Close is never used as an executable trade price. DECISION_REQUIRED_ETF_DIVIDEND_TREATMENT (whether *execution* prices reflect dividend adjustment) is a separate, still-open decision, untouched by this resolution. DECISION_REQUIRED_LOOKBACK_N and DECISION_REQUIRED_VOLUME_INPUT remain open and continue to block src/tensors.py::build_paper_tensor.

topic: Whether the final reported model includes ETF volume
source_evidence: p.3 footnote: tensor is N x (2l+m) 'if ETF volumes are used in the analysis' -- conditional, never resolved for the final Table 3 model.
why_it_matters: Doubles the traded-asset feature block (l -> 2l) if included; changes model input width and every downstream shape.

candidate_options.description: PRICE_ONLY (volume excluded from final model)
candidate_options.source_support: The 'final results... based only on model inputs comprising the sector funds' sentence most naturally reads as price-only, though it does not explicitly disclaim volume.

candidate_options.description: PRICE_PLUS_VOLUME
candidate_options.source_support: Footnote explicitly allows for this configuration; Discussion section (p.6) also refers to 'a function connecting prices and volumes... with their future values', which is explicit textual support for volume being part of the *final* model, in tension with option A.

resolution.outcome: RESOLVED by explicit user instruction, not by inference upgrade -- source_classification stays MISSING (the paper never states, for the *final* Table 3 model specifically, whether the conditional 'N x (2l+m) if ETF volumes are used' footnote condition held). The final reported model INCLUDES ETF volume as a model input: l=11, m=0 (auxiliary economic variables remain excluded, unchanged), so the canonical per-week input width is 2l+m = 22 (11 price columns + 11 volume columns). User rationale (recorded for provenance): the footnote explicitly allows this configuration, and the Discussion section's 'a function connecting prices and volumes... with their future values' is explicit textual support for volume surviving into the final model, in tension with a PRICE_ONLY reading of the 'based only on model inputs comprising the sector funds of Table 1' sentence (which most naturally resolves *auxiliary* variables m, not volume of the traded assets themselves).

volume_sampling_rule.classification_note: Strongly supported by the paper but not literally explicit -- must NOT be relabeled PAPER_EXPLICIT.
volume_sampling_rule.formula: volume_input[s,t] = Yahoo daily Volume from the FINAL ACTUAL TRADING SESSION of week t. Normal week -> Friday daily Volume. Friday market holiday -> Thursday daily Volume. Other shortened week -> Volume from that week's final actual trading session. Sampled from the exact same model_cutoff date already used for price (src/calendar.py), never a literal-Friday assumption.
supporting_paper_evidence: Price and volume data for each ETF were acquired from Yahoo Finance (p.3, S2.1).
Sector ETF data were sampled at discrete points in time and filtered to weekly Friday-close observations (p.3, S2.1).
Training examples described as matrices containing 'prices, volumes and other data recorded for the current and previous N-1 weeks' (p.3, S2.1).
Footnote: input dimensions are N x (2l+m) 'if ETF volumes are used' (p.3, S2.1).
Figure 1 explicitly states volumes are omitted from the schematic for clarity, not absent from the model (p.4).
Discussion describes the model as learning relationships connecting prices and volumes across economic sectors with future values (p.6).
No source evidence found for weekly sum, weekly mean, weekly aggregation, cumulative volume, rolling volume, or any other volume transformation.

final_input_geometry.tensor_shape: X_t in R^(N x 22), N unresolved (DECISION_REQUIRED_LOOKBACK_N)

canonical_column_order.ordering_convention: Grouped [all prices, all volumes], NOT ticker-by-ticker interleaved -- no paper evidence supports an interleaved arrangement, so this grouped order is a deterministic implementation convention, hard-asserted in src/tensors.py::assert_canonical_market_columns / MARKET_COLUMNS.

resolution.normalization: Each of the 22 columns z-scored independently using the already-resolved DECISION_REQUIRED_NORMALIZATION_SCOPE policy: per-ETF, fit once on the annual model's initial two-year training window [Y-2, Y), ddof=0, then frozen for the trading year. Volume never shares mu/sigma with price, different ETFs, or different annual models -- src/normalization.py::fit_annual_volume_scaler.
resolution.missing_data_policy: A missing/invalid final-session Volume for a ticker/week is never forward-filled, backfilled, interpolated, zero-substituted, or weekly-average-substituted -- raises src/tensors.py::MissingVolumeDataError, an explicit auditable data-integrity error.
resolution.note: Does NOT resolve DECISION_REQUIRED_LOOKBACK_N (tensor depth N), which remains USER_DECISION_REQUIRED and continues to block src/tensors.py::build_paper_tensor. Does NOT alter DECISION_REQUIRED_PRICE_FIELD, DECISION_REQUIRED_TARGET_RETURN_INTERVAL, DECISION_REQUIRED_HOLIDAY_EXECUTION, or DECISION_REQUIRED_NORMALIZATION_SCOPE -- all remain exactly as previously resolved. Volume is a model INPUT only, never used as an execution price and never a model output/target (MIMO output geometry remains 11).

topic: Exact date range the +1% label return is measured over
source_evidence: p.3: '...implicitly predict two distinct future values (Monday open and Friday close)'; p.4-5 execution timeline confirms Mon-open entry / Fri-close exit.
why_it_matters: Changes every label in the entire dataset; a Fri-close-to-Fri-close definition captures weekend gap risk the strategy never actually trades, while Mon-open-to-Fri-close matches the tradeable P&L exactly.

candidate_options.description: next Monday open -> next Friday close (matches realized tradeable return)
candidate_options.source_support: STRONG_INFERENCE from the 'two distinct future values' sentence plus the execution timeline.

candidate_options.description: current Friday close -> next Friday close
candidate_options.source_support: Simpler, common convention in weekly-bar literature; contradicts the 'two distinct future values' phrasing if adopted literally, since it only involves one future value (next Friday close).

resolution.option_chosen: A, generalized to actual trading sessions
resolution.outcome: RESOLVED by explicit user instruction, not by inference upgrade -- the paper source evidence remains STRONG_INFERENCE only (never an equation in the source text); the interval itself is a USER-RESOLVED reconstruction decision, distinct from the +100bps/+1% threshold, which remains PAPER EXPLICIT. Exact definition: target_trade_return[s,t+1] = final_actual_trading_day_close[s,t+1] / first_actual_trading_day_open[s,t+1] - 1, where 'first/final actual trading day' is the target week's first/last day actually present in the observed trading calendar (not a literal Monday/Friday) -- applies uniformly to normal and holiday-shortened weeks. target[s,t+1] = 1 iff target_trade_return[s,t+1] >= 0.01, else 0 (TARGET_THRESHOLD_BPS, unchanged, EXPLICIT). Implemented in src/labels.py::build_paper_labels, consuming src/calendar.py's entry_candidate_date (first actual trading day of week t+1) and label_known_date (last actual trading day of week t+1) columns -- both already computed generically from real observed trading days, so no separate holiday-substitution logic was needed. This resolution also settles DECISION_REQUIRED_HOLIDAY_EXECUTION for the weekly entry/exit session-selection question specifically -- see that decision's own resolution block.
resolution.note: Resolves label/execution TIMING only. DECISION_REQUIRED_PRICE_FIELD (what price field feeds the model's input tensor X_t) is NOT resolved by this decision and remains USER_DECISION_REQUIRED -- raw executable Open/Close used for the target label does not imply raw Close (or any other field) is used for the model input.

topic: Scope over which zero-mean/unit-variance normalization stats are computed
source_evidence: p.3: 'All non-target data were normalized to have zero mean and unit variance' -- states the transform, not its scope.
why_it_matters: Determines whether normalization stats are refreshed weekly (expanding/rolling) or fixed per annual training window; also determines lookahead-safety implementation detail.

candidate_options.description: Fit once per trading year on the 2-year training window, held fixed through all weekly updates that year
candidate_options.source_support: Consistent with 'individual models trained... for trading years' cadence, but not stated for normalization specifically.

candidate_options.description: Refit weekly on an expanding window (all data through the most recent observed week)
candidate_options.source_support: Consistent with 'dynamic update' framing applied to the whole pipeline, but not stated for normalization specifically.

candidate_options.description: Refit weekly on a fixed-size rolling window of the most recent N weeks (same N as the tensor depth)
candidate_options.source_support: No direct textual support.

resolution.option_chosen: A, restated exactly, with explicit per-ETF (column-wise) axis
resolution.outcome: RESOLVED by explicit user instruction, not by inference upgrade -- source_classification stays MISSING (the paper states the z-score transform generally but never its scope/axis/cadence). Column-wise / per-ETF z-score: mu[s,Y] and sigma[s,Y] are each ETF's own mean/std over that annual model's initial two-year training history only (11 means + 11 stds for the price-only case, never one pooled statistic across ETFs). Z[s,t,Y] = (AdjustedClose[s,t] - mu[s,Y]) / sigma[s,Y]. Fit window = the SAME initial 2-year window ([Y-2, Y)) the annual model itself trains on (reusing src/training_schedule.py::AnnualScheduler.training_window_for_year, already EXPLICIT p.3 'previous 2 years' -- not re-derived). Frozen for the entire trading year Y: no weekly refit, no expanding/rolling update during weekly predictions or weekly incremental model updates; a new trading year Y+1 gets an entirely new scaler fit from its own preceding 2-year window. ddof=0 (population variance, matching the project's pre-existing generic fit_normalization() convention -- not a new, separate convention). Zero/negligible training-window variance for a ticker raises ZeroVarianceTrainingWindowError (identifying year/ticker/sigma) rather than silently defaulting sigma=1. Implemented in src/normalization.py::AnnualPriceScaler / fit_annual_price_scaler.
resolution.note: User rationale (recorded for provenance, not paper-explicit): weekly scaler updates would change the coordinate system underneath model weights already trained in the previous normalized space; the frozen-annual approach instead preserves stable feature coordinates, strict no-lookahead, annual-model consistency, and compatibility with weekly continuation/update of the same model weights. DECISION_REQUIRED_LOOKBACK_N (tensor depth N) remains open -- the scaler operates on the weekly price panel directly and does not require N to be resolved; the normalized tensor builder remains parameterized by N. DECISION_REQUIRED_VOLUME_INPUT remains open; if later approved, volume gets its own independent mean/std, never shared with price statistics. DECISION_REQUIRED_WEEKLY_UPDATE_MECHANISM remains open; any weekly sample fed into the annual model during year Y must be transformed with this same frozen scaler, regardless of the eventual update mechanism.

resolution.outcome: RESOLVED as a direct consequence of the user's DECISION_REQUIRED_TARGET_RETURN_INTERVAL resolution, which is the same underlying question for weekly entry/exit SESSION SELECTION: entry = first actual trading day of the target week (Tuesday if Monday is a holiday); exit = last actual trading day of the target week (Thursday if Friday is a holiday). This is mechanically equivalent to option A ('nearest following trading day for a missing Monday' / 'nearest prior trading day for a missing Friday'). Audited against the rest of this register and docs/paper_execution_timeline.md, docs/paper_source_audit.md #5: no other, independent holiday question was found under this decision_id (e.g. risk-rule evaluation cadence and the SPX benchmark series do not reference DECISION_REQUIRED_HOLIDAY_EXECUTION) -- so this decision is resolved in full, not split.
resolution.note: Implemented in src/calendar.py, which already computed first_actual_trading_day/last_actual_trading_day generically from the real observed trading-day index (not from a literal Monday/Friday assumption); only the blocking guard (previously src/calendar.py::require_holiday_decision_if_incomplete, raised on friday_present == False) was removed, since that condition no longer represents an unresolved decision.

resolution.outcome: FRAMEWORK_SUBSTITUTION_NOT_REQUIRED -- a dedicated Python 3.13.13 environment (.venvs/deep_sector_rotation/, see research/strategies/deep_sector_rotation_paper_rebuild/requirements.txt) was provisioned with TensorFlow 2.21.0 and Keras 3.15.1 installed and verified importable. tests/test_model_architecture.py::test_build_model_produces_correct_layer_sequence_and_output_shape now runs and passes (previously skipped for lack of TensorFlow). PyTorch (option B) was never used.
resolution.note: This resolves only the framework/environment decision. All other Level 1/2/3 decisions in this register remain USER_DECISION_REQUIRED; the rebuild remains PAPER_REBUILD_BLOCKED_ON_USER_DECISIONS overall.
